text:
Priya Shah: Heads up — we got an invoice for March that includes a mid-month reserved capacity adjustment plus burst charges for AcuSense (INV-2026-03-78). Can someone confirm why the reserved commit was prorated instead of moving to a target allocation?
Liam O'Connor: i pulled the allocation logs — looks like a pool rebalance on 03/12 triggered a partial decommit and then a re-reserve. system treated the re-reserve as new capacity = prorate.
Carlos Mendez: @Priya can you paste the invoice lines? I want to check how they billed the burst vs commit bucket.
Priya Shah: here are the relevant lines from the PDF extract: 
```
Line 42: Reserved capacity (monthly) - AcuSense - 0.6 -> billed 0.6 for Mar12-31 = $7,200
Line 43: Reserved capacity adjustment - re-reserve 0.4 (Mar1-11) - prorate credit applied = -$1,850
Line 78: Burst overage - peak GPU hours - Mar12-13 - 18.6 hours = $2,220
INV total: $7,570 (net)
```
Marta Liu: tagging finance ops — the policy says if a customer reassigns capacity within the same month we should apply a transfer not a decommit/prorate unless there's an explicit cancellation request. Do we have a change request from AcuSense?
Liam O'Connor: there was an automated orchestration job (autoscale-scheduler) that moved VMs between pools during a maintenance window; no manual cancellation. I can pull the event id.
Priya Shah: AcuSense engineering submitted a support ticket (SUP-6291) saying they requested a smaller commit on the 10th, but the timing looks funky — their account rep (Carlos) approved on the 12th. Ticket timestamps attached in the portal.
Carlos Mendez: i approved a smaller commit because they asked for cost reallocation to a different team. My notes: "approve 0.6->0.4 commit, effective 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC" — but the system shows decommit at 00:30 and re-reserve at 04:12. clearly the autoscaler raced with the account change.
Marta Liu: OK — root cause is race between the customer-requested commit change and the autoscaler. Finance policy allows a one-time manual adjustment (credit) if the decommit was unintentional and the customer requested the change before the autoscaler action. We need evidence of the request time + account rep approval. Carlos can you confirm the approval timestamp?
Carlos Mendez: confirmed — approval recorded at 03:05 UTC. I also have the signed change email from the customer at 02:58 UTC.
Priya Shah: I propose issuing a corrective adjustment: convert the prorate credit + reapply the reserved capacity as a transfer so net customer charge equals continuous 0.4 from Mar1-31 (i.e., full month pricing for 0.4 plus burst where applicable). Rough calc: reverse the prorate credit (-$1,850), apply 0.2-month credit to adjust to 0.4 for full month (-$2,400), then reclassify burst hours (reduce by ~12 GPU-hours) -> net credit ~$1,300.
Marta Liu: I'm good with that approach but need approval from finance lead. @billing-bot please create an adjustment request doc with supporting artifacts: SUP-6291, email sig, account rep note, autoscaler event logs.
billing-bot: Adjustment request created: ADJ-2026-4481. Attached artifacts: SUP-6291, acusense-change-emails.pdf, autoscale-events-03-12.log, account-notes. Status: awaiting finance lead review.
Liam O'Connor: putting the autoscale event snippet below for audit: 
```
2026-03-12T00:30:12Z autoscale-scheduler: pool-decommit vm-pool-east-23 reason: node_maintenance
2026-03-12T03:02:58Z user-request: AcuSense change_request id=CR-3412
2026-03-12T03:05:10Z account-action: Carlos Mendez approve CR-3412
2026-03-12T04:12:47Z autoscale-scheduler: pool-reserve vm-pool-east-23 reason: rebalance
```
Priya Shah: That should be enough evidence. Marta — do you want me to draft the adjustment memo for the ledger?
Marta Liu: yes pls. include the net credit calc, links to ADJ-2026-4481, and note that customer-facing communication will be "billing correction for overlapping change & autoscale event". I'll review and sign.
Carlos Mendez: i'll handle customer comms once finance approves. lean toward offering a short apology and the net $1,300 credit applied to next invoice.
Priya Shah: draft done, pushed to ADJ-2026-4481 doc. pinging @Marta for final sign-off.
Marta Liu: reviewed and signed off. please post the adjustment to the ledger and file the reversal journal. Finance ops: can you schedule the credit for the Apr billing run?
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4481 status updated: approved_by_finance. Scheduled for execution in billing run 2026-04-03. Journal entry: JE-2026-7782.
Priya Shah: thanks team. note for postmortem: add a guardrail so account changes within 6h of autoscaler events get queued for manual reconcile to avoid double-billing. I'll create a GH issue. :memo:
Carlos Mendez: +1. Also will ask product to add an "in-flight change" flag on account edits.
Marta Liu: closing loop — customer notified, credit scheduled, docs attached to ADJ-2026-4481. leaving this thread to archive. :white_check_mark:
